questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose UC Berkeley as my exchange destination for one because my brother lived an hour away. Another crucial point was the level of education that I expected from the institution I visited. UC in general is known for being a group of universities with a higher academic level than usual, and Berkeley, which I visited, has a very great academic reputation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
While the academic level of UC Berkeley was very high, that was mostly felt in the research department. The research department received most of the funding available, which left the education part rather underfunded and as a result made the courses resource strained. This was evident in the fact that the courses, while requiring much more work as a result of a very high workload, did not necessarily explore much more material than covered in the respective courses at KU.

However, and I cannot stress this enough, what made my exchange experience the most worthwhile was the relationship I got with my professors. Your education at Berkeley and the rest of the UC locations will be greatly improved if you go to office hours with the professors and the TAs. This made for many interesting discussions and learning much more outside the curriculum.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It depends on how much you've prepared beforehand. The US isn't known for its fantastic public infrastructure and it shows. The university is great at giving information about the university itself, the campus and its surroundings, and the local amenities, but outside that sphere you're on your own. I highly recommend preparing beforehand, such as reading about the public transport available and downloading Uber of Lyft beforehand just in case, and having a way of using data in the US before you take off.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received help from the university most parts in relation to the covid situation in Berkeley. Omicron was raging at that time and given I had just landed I knew nothing about the situation or how I should go about dealing with it. I recommend getting in touch with the university if you have questions!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The university was very helpful in introducing me to the institution and the local surroundings. You have a a couple of introduction days where you meet other exchange students and get to know the campus and the students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Listen, housing in Berkeley is expensive. For a single room around 10 minutes on bike away from campus I paid around 12000 kr. per month (some 1700 odd USD). The university tries to find housing for everyone, but did state that it will not be able to find housing for everyone. I got lucky with Airbnb and suggest you at least try, since many places have long term renting available at good (for Berkeley) prices.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can drink alcohol off campus, even if the housing is provided by the university. Other than that it is not at all bad to live off campus since Berkeley is very much a college town and college oriented stuff happens outside campus as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy if you're early.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have an online portal where you register and you can even add courses to a shopping cart beforehand so you can sign up to all the desired courses as soon as the registration period opens. I got all of the courses is wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you want help, you can always email the school registations service or individual professors regarding their course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Yes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register early so you can get all the courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was about the same as KU, but the workload (at least in science) was much higher. I had a course going for 15 weeks with 12 homework, 6 quizzes, a programming assignment, a midterm, and a final exam. All this for what amounted to 9 ects. In other studies the workload will be higher but not to the same degree, as science was known to have a hard workload.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There was a larger focus on interaction with the professors. We had professors constantly tell us to approach them if we had issues, and one professor sent mails to each of the students that did not pass the midterm to ask them what they struggled with and if they wanted to come to office hours.

It also takes a lot more work to learn the same material, as evident in the example earlier, for which the material was the same as the material in the KU equivalent course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Math 128A - Numerical Analysis
Math 105 - Second Course In Analysis
Stat 153 - Time Series Analysis
Stat 33b - Introduction to Advanced R

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Avoid Math 128A at all costs. You'll get much more out of numerical analysis at KU and you'll still have your sanity afterwards.

Stat 153 was incredibly good, I highly recommend that to anyone interested. The professor was very committed to teaching us and making us understand the topics, and the homework, while long, was very good as it added additional understanding of the topics taught.

Math 105 was also very good and has the added benefit of being a smaller course where you can really get to know the professor. He is very interested in the subjects and going to his office was very rewarding. It was also participation based *chefs kiss*.

Stat 33b, if you want to learn R, is very good. I did not anticipate going from thinking so little of R to thinking so highly of it. Goes to show that a good teacher can completely change your perspective of a topic or programming language.

questions.answer: It was not unexpected, but Americans and their insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I did not anticipate housing being that expensive. I know some that paid 35.000 DKK for a two bedroom apartment. Ouch.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything you could think of. For clubs they had sports, gaming, consulting, coding, charity, painting, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Berkeley als has something called a DeCal which I wish I knew before I chose courses. They are courses started by students with the counselling of a professor. I put these under non-academic as some of the deCals included "introduction to tea", "Introduction to Poker", "The Nature of Pixar Films", and the all time favorite: "Learn to Play the Sather Tower Bells", where you learn to play the bells of the Sather Tower in the middle of the campus. Check out
https://decal.berkeley.edu/courses
for more.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking, climbing, sailing or something else. California is all about the nature and being outside, and if you're danish, you're not gonna get that at home, so use the nature while you can!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Being danish, there really isn't that big of a difference. Americans are much more open, and if you ever talk to one on the street it is not uncommon to be invited to dinner or to join their communist activist group (actually happened). Once you get used to the openness of the locals, everything is easy enough to get used to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the bars or to the club fair! Talk to other students in class, or meet people in the dining halls. Just talk to other students, its incredible how easy it is to find friends that way.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Guns and safety. We had a 45 min introduction to safety in the area where we were told to always watch our surroundings as muggings, even downtown in populated areas were not uncommon. Always walk in groups and avoid suspicious people. They had a campus police station, which came in handy quite a lot as there was at least a mugging or an assault a week.

In terms of guns, some americans hated them, some loved them. But the fact that most people shrugged at a local school shooting because they were so common what unfathomable to me. Get used to the guns, especially when travelling outside a major city.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of the americans were amazing. Americans are always friendly (Unless they're from NYC).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take breaks and use them to enjoy the nature, do not concern yourself with the food quality, and try to talk to as many people as possible!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend finding a place to live before arriving. And if/when you feel homesick, know that it is okay. We all feel it, and it is natural to miss home after such a long period away. Remind yourself of it when you get back home.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of studying at such a major institution was amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academical pressure at the university is difficult to handle. A lot of students end up doing nothing but school work for 14-15 weeks straight due to the pressure to perform. Homesickness as well, especially because they don't have adequate rye bread and greek yoghurt is subpar.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
